evidence: Figure 1: Running Examples. (a) Point-Mass Docking: Here, a point mass must pass through a channel and cross the dock line within speed and lateral position limits. The line plots in (a) depict traces from trial runs under two different control settings: a base policy (red) and a control scheme where control of the point-mass’s acceleration is switched to a state-feedback controller in the channel phase (blue). In each setting, we use the same initial state, physical parameters, and noise draws. Under the base policy, the point mass exceeds the speed limit at the dock line. With state-feedback acceleration commands in the channel (blue), it satisfies both terminal limits. Open circles mark phase starts. The dotted curve gives the speed bound for one-dimensional braking without drag or noise. (b,c) Bimanual Robotic Assembly: In this task, we require a bimanual robotic manipulator to insert a key-like part with its right hand into a housing stabilized by the left hand. The part must remain stable in the housing after the robot withdraws its hands. The frames in the figure show an episode under the state-feedback controller in Isaac Lab ( Mittal et al., 2023 ) .
